metadata.title: KNN Classification Platform
metadata.description: Interactive platform for evaluating K-Nearest Neighbors classification with exact and approximate (HNSW) vector search in PostgreSQL + pgvector.

overview.title: Research overview
overview.subtitle: Exact vs. approximate nearest-neighbour retrieval for KNN classification
overview.question: Research question
overview.questionBody: Can approximate nearest-neighbour search in PostgreSQL improve the performance of a KNN classification system while maintaining acceptable classification quality?
overview.noData: No experiments yet. Ingest a dataset and run the exact baseline to get started.
overview.step1: Ingest the UCI Covertype dataset (or upload your own CSV).
overview.step2: Run the exact baseline to establish the reference accuracy.
overview.step3: Run HNSW with several ef_search values to map the recall / latency trade-off.
overview.step4: Compare both approaches side by side.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.subtitle: How the platform is built and measured
methodology.step2: Preprocessing fitted on the training split only
methodology.step3: Feature vectors written to a dimensionally-typed pgvector table
methodology.step4: Exact retrieval produces the ground-truth neighbour set
methodology.step5: HNSW retrieval reuses the same query with the index enabled
methodology.step6: Majority voting classifies; metrics are computed and persisted
methodology.metricClassification: Classification — accuracy, macro precision / recall / F1
methodology.metricRetrieval: Retrieval — Recall@K against the exact neighbour set
methodology.metricLatency: Latency — average, median, p95 and p99 per query
methodology.metricIndex: Index — HNSW construction time and detected access path
methodology.noteExact: The exact baseline uses the pgvector distance function, which can never be satisfied by an index, guaranteeing an exhaustive scan.
methodology.noteIsolation: Each dataset owns a dedicated vector table with a fixed dimension, which is required by pgvector for a usable HNSW index and keeps neighbours isolated per dataset.
methodology.noteWarmup: The first query of each run is executed twice and discarded, so the reported latency excludes first-call planning and cold-cache effects.
